editorial.headline: A Nationally Open Trade That Bali Blocks
editorial.standfirst: Used-motorcycle wholesale is nationally open to full foreign ownership across all listed business scales, yet Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium prevents registration there.
editorial.body:
At its core, this is wholesale trade in used motorcycles—a category that also includes motorised bicycles and mopeds. It is a focused trading activity, defined by the fact that the motorcycles are used and by the wholesale character of the transaction. The commercial subject is second-hand motorcycles, with motorised bicycles and mopeds expressly within the same activity. For a business selecting the classification, the practical reading begins and ends with that defined field of trade.

Nationally, the activity is marked TERBUKA and carries a maximum foreign-ownership position of 100% under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In direct terms, the national setting permits full foreign ownership for this activity. It is open at every listed scale—Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar—so the classification is not confined to one size of enterprise. That breadth establishes the national position across the listed scales, but it does not erase the separate Bali position.

For PMA, a foreigner cannot register this activity in Bali today. The Bali status is blocked by risk class: at the Besar scale, its OSS risk assessment is Low or Medium-Low across every scope, bringing it within Bali’s island-wide, permanent PMA moratorium for those risk levels. This is not a lower Bali foreign-ownership ceiling. The national ceiling remains 100%, while the provincial rule blocks the PMA registration route. The record identifies the moratorium as dating from May 2026 and cites Governor’s letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. The distinction is decisive: national foreign-ownership openness is real, but it does not create a Bali PMA registration path for this activity.
